findings.finding: r7 authorization_rule gate1 (git log --branches --not --remotes -- <path> empty) is UNREACHABLE in any repo with zero remote-tracking refs: every commit ever made is listed, so no obsidian-class ticket can ever pass gate1-as-written. Observed: vaultmove fixture (1 commit, no remote) lists its only commit; yet toolA/toolB agree SAFE moved-to-obsidian. Amendment used: when refs/remotes is empty, gate1 substitutes toolB VERIFIED(moved-to-obsidian) (source+vault digests re-hash) as the unpushed-half. Live-fleet consequence: the lane's dead origin (r7: 404) blocks obsidian tickets for TRACKED files exactly as it blocks pushed tickets.

r7 authorization_rule gate2 (status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- <path> empty) forbids every UNTRACKED candidate by definition — an untracked scratch file always prints '?? <path>'. Observed: stale fixture shows gate2v1 non-empty while toolA/toolB agree SAFE stale. Amendment used: gate2-prime = porcelain excluding untracked ('?? ') lines (tracked dirt only); untracked-ness is the stale ticket's own substance, re-checked by refs=0. Live-fleet consequence: lore-shokunin/.scratch and kotodama-shokunin/.scratch style candidates were auto-denied by r7 text even where the tool receipts agreed.

tool receipts alone are NOT sufficient for authorization: toolA emits SAFE(pushed) for a file with UNCOMMITTED worktree modifications (fixture docs/q11-dirty.md: clean history, dirty worktree -> try_pushed never inspects the worktree). The r7 gate2 layer is what catches it. Observed: control-dirty — toolA SAFE/pushed, gate2 non-empty, runner refused. Keep gates AND tools in step_0_recheck; never collapse to tool-only.

Staging via plain mv PRESERVES mtime and basename, so a stale-class staged copy still verifies SAFE(stale) under the mangled path (observed: flow-stale-staged-verdict SAFE/stale), while pushed/obsidian-class staged copies verify NOT-SAFE (their receipts are history/ledger-bound to the original path; observed: NOT-SAFE/none on both). The staged copy therefore carries NO independent authorization — the ticket authorization is derived pre-stage from the original path and the second check must gate on byte-identity + gate stability, exactly as implemented.

Quarantining a TRACKED path leaves an unstaged deletion (' D <path>') in the lane worktree after step_4 (observed in flow-pushed-final / flow-obsidian-final). The r7 template's 'no index churn' mv is correct for staging but the runbook must add an operator-visible close-out: record the deletion receipt in LOG.md; the parent decides when the deletion is committed. Untracked (stale-class) staging leaves the worktree clean (observed: flow-stale-final clean).

Live dry-run probe confirms the r7 boundary stands: toolA on live lane paths returns NOT-SAFE with evidence pushed-unverifiable (refs/remotes empty, origin 404). The ONLY gate-opening move that is operator-owned for the pushed class: create/restore the lane origin and push master; every other class (stale/obsidian/metadata-prune) is blocked by live citations, digest-less ledger, locked/unique worktree state, or dirty trees.
